note: Borders: historical-basemaps by André Ourednik (GitHub aourednik/historical-basemaps, commit da7a4b7 of 15 Sep 2026, GPL-3.0). The project marks every border as approximate (BORDERPRECISION 1) and asks users to check it against other sources. Orbis clipped the maps to the regions its stories show, simplified them and grouped the polygons into states (drawn with borders) and peoples, cultures and nomadic groups (drawn as soft areas: their extent is an estimate). Maps used: AD 800 (Europe), 1000 (Anatolia and the Caucasus), 1279, 1400, 1492 and 1530 (eastern Mediterranean and Near East), 1815 (only the Austrian Empire: the source's 1815 map draws Frankfurt, Hamburg, Bremen and Lübeck inside neighbouring states and Thuringia as one state). Shown: 800 until 843 (Treaty of Verdun); 1000 until 1045 (Byzantium annexes Bagratid Armenia); 1279 until 1300; 1400 until 1453; 1492 from 1453 (Constantinople Ottoman; the source's 1500 map is the same here) until 1516; 1530 from 1516 (Mamluk Syria and Egypt conquered); 1815 until 1866. Corrections: 'Seljuk Caliphate' (1279) is shown as the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum; the 1400 map's Seljuk state in eastern Anatolia is left out (the sultanate had ended by 1308); 'Bulgar Khanate' is shown as the Bulgarian Empire (1000, 1279) and Ottoman Bulgaria (1400). Not used: the source's 1100 and 1200 maps, which still draw Byzantium across all of Anatolia (the Seljuks held its centre from the 1070s). This derived file is distributed under the GNU GPL v3, like its source.
